summary:
After 16 experiments on the oxford-camera-holdout tuning set, the gate constraint max_false_alarms_per_hour <= 0.0 is the persistent blocker: every configuration produces ~37 false alarms per hour, far exceeding the limit of 0.0. All other metrics (recall >= 1.0 for all fault types, detection/recovery seconds within [0, 2.0] bounds, max_age_s <= 0.5, unknown_fraction <= 0.1, unfinished frames == 0) pass when false alarms are ignored.

Key observations across configs:
- Baseline (threads=1, sample_every=1, queue_size=2): cpu_seconds_per_camera_second = 0.2312
- threads=2, queue_size=2: cpu = 0.2390 (slightly higher)
- sample_every=2, queue_size=2: cpu = 0.2163 but max_age_s inflates to ~0.208 (still under 0.5 limit)
- threads=4, queue_size=2: cpu = 0.2692 (worse)
- queue_size=1: cpu = 0.2313, similar to baseline
- queue_size=4: cpu = 0.2319, max_age_s spikes to 0.214

No configuration achieved max_false_alarms_per_hour <= 0.0; the false alarms remain ~37/hr across all parameter combinations. Since gates must pass entirely, no tuning of processing parameters alone can meet the false alarm constraint. Detector tuning (glare_rise, dark_ratio, blur_ratio, obstruction_ratio, hysteresis, persistence_s, recovery_s) was not varied in these runs; the baseline detector null kept the original threshold suite.

Given the mandatory gate requirement and the false alarm floor at ~37/hr, the search space under current knobs (width∈{320,640,960,1280}, sample_every∈{1,2,4}, threads∈{1,2,4}, queue_size∈{1,2,4}) yields no passing configuration. Further work would need to address the false alarm source (e.g., detector threshold adjustments, algorithmic changes) outside the permitted parameter set.

experiments.rationale: Measure the reference configuration before search.
